Subject: Order Form: early-exit smoothing, cap matrix & trigger mechanics — redlines

Hi Laura / Markus,

Attaching the latest order form and appendix B pricing matrix from Brightline (they sent v3 this morning). Legal flagged a few items in the pricing exhibits that need commercial input before we send back a consolidated redline:

- Early-exit smoothing: they want a pro-rata true-up based on a 12-month lookback and a %-of-commit cap. That reads like a full refund in some scenarios; we should consider a tapering schedule to protect unit economics.
- Cap matrix anomalies: Appendix B lists an effective per-embedding cap that flips at odd thresholds (e.g., 250k -> 255k) — appears to create a cliff around the quarterly measurement period.
- Trigger mechanics: they propose an "auto-stabilizer" that pauses overage billing when monthly utilization drops >40% MoM; product thinks this will complicate billing and game the smoothing window.

Ask: can you review these three areas with a recommended redline for each (word-level language) and confirm whether we can accept a 90-day smoothing window and a soft cap that scales linearly rather than stepwise? I want to get a clean consolidated redline back to Emily by Thursday COB (2027-06-24).

Attachments: OrderForm_Brightline_v3.docx, PricingMatrix_AppendixB.xlsx

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick heads-up. Attached is Brightline's proposed redline (BR_redline_v3_marked.docx). A few clarifications on their position so your team has context:

1) Early-exit smoothing: they propose a 12-month lookback to compute a "smoothing credit" applied to final invoice; the intent is to prevent double-charging in seasonal drop-offs. They believe a 12-month window is fair given their seasonal cycles.

2) Cap matrix: the cliff you noted is intentional; they say the band widths align with internal product usage buckets. They offered to make the bands wider but are unwilling to move to a continuous formula unless we accept a minimum guaranteed commit.

3) Trigger mechanics: the "auto-stabilizer" is intended as a consumer protection — it pauses overage billing during an abrupt customer shutdown (e.g., if an integration was disabled). They're open to a shorter lookback for the trigger (they suggested 30 days) if we can accept the pause.

We redlined alternative text in the doc where we think a middle ground is possible (see comments). If you're going to propose a 90-day smoothing window and a linearized cap, please confirm commercial tradeoffs so I can advise Brightline counsel.

Best,
Emily Lawson
Counsel, Brightline Health
(emily@brightlinelegal.com)

Karthik / Markus,

I reviewed Brightline's redline and Emily's notes. My suggested counterpoints (word-level bullets you can drop into the consolidated redline):

- Early-exit smoothing: propose "Smoothing Window = 90 days (net of any force majeure) where a credit is calculated as the difference between invoiced usage and contracted baseline for the smoothing window, capped at 25% of the remaining committed fees." This keeps us from full refunds while offering them a buffer for short seasonal drops.

- Cap matrix: replace stepwise bands with a linearized per-unit rate for the band between 100k and 1M units: Rate = BaseRate + ((Usage - LowerBound) / (UpperBound - LowerBound)) * Spread. Add a hard floor equal to 60% of BaseRate and a hard ceiling equal to 130% of BaseRate to protect us from outliers.

- Trigger mechanics: accept a 30-day emergency pause but only where the customer attests to a documented outage or integration disablement and with a one-time cap of 2 pause events per 12-month term. Also require Customer to notify Redwood within 5 business days and provide supporting evidence.

Commercial tradeoffs: 90-day smoothing increases our short-term churn exposure slightly but protects churned customers from billing disputes; the linearized cap smooths revenue recognition but reduces short-term upside from band cliffs.

If you agree, I'll draft the consolidated language and produce a single "Consolidated_Redline_BR_20270624.docx".

- Laura
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference

Emily / Brightline team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on your redline. Per internal review we've prepared a single consolidated redline (Consolidated_Redline_BR_20270624.docx) that captures our proposed compromise. Summary of the key changes: 

1) Early-exit smoothing: Smoothing Window = 90 days; smoothing credit capped at 25% of remaining committed fees; formula language included in Section 4 of the Pricing Exhibit.
2) Cap matrix: replaced the discrete cliff bands with a linearized rate formula between adjacent band bounds; hard floor = 60% BaseRate; hard ceiling = 130% BaseRate.
3) Trigger mechanics: emergency pause allowed up to 2 events per 12-month period, requires written notice within 5 business days and evidence; pause does not retroactively waive fees beyond the smoothing window.

Attachments: Consolidated_Redline_BR_20270624.docx (word-level redline) and a clean copy of the PricingMatrix_AppendixB.xlsx showing the linearized sample rates.

Please confirm by COB Monday 2027-06-28 if these changes are acceptable or propose alternative wording where you still have concerns. If you prefer a call, I'm available Friday morning PT.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts
